latin: Ad probandum primam materiam esse, magis certificat uel uia numerorum, uel uia catholicae philosophiae, quam ulla ratio physica in qua sensus habeat introitum.
translation: To prove that prime matter exists, either the way of numbers or the way of universal philosophy gives more certainty than any physical argument in which sense-perception has an entry.
translation_note: 'catholicae philosophiae' is rendered 'universal philosophy'; 'catholicae' here means 'universal', not the later confessional sense (farmer1998:21090).
